title: Premature Consistent Hashing on Fixed Clusters
pattern: Implementing a complex consistent hash ring with virtual nodes for distributing data across a small, static set of database connections or servers.
why_bad: Consistent hashing adds lookup latency and code complexity to calculate ranges and virtual node maps. If the set of nodes is fixed and small, a simple modulo lookup (`hash(key) % server_count`) is hundreds of times faster, fully balanced, and trivially simple to implement [300].
detection: Complex consistent hashing library usage or custom hash ring implementation when the connection pool or server list size is static and known at build time.
counterexample: Dynamically scaled caching clusters (such as Memcached pools with dozens of nodes) where nodes are added or removed multiple times a day. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Use a simple static key index hashing modulo connection length.
